answer: A reputation score can be made perishable: it decays every epoch unless the identity posts a fresh, verifiable judgment call that no other account can reuse. A sybil farm can clone names, but not repeated acts of discernment—like a poet drafting a new sonnet each morning rather than photocopying yesterday’s; like a lagoon whose inlet must be fed by tide or it turns stagnant; like a nebula that dims unless new starlight sustains it. Each fake persona must independently bear that renewal cost, so multiplying accounts multiplies work, not trust.
